A5169672.story: Tabasco is a tiny dog carrying a lot of fear. He bonded with the person who found him and was gentle with her kids, but the shelter has pushed him past his limits. What looks like aggression is terror with no exit.
A5169672.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Tabasco needs a quiet foster home with no other dogs, no children, and an experienced handler who understands fear-based behavior and will not rush him. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than August 19th.

A5169682.name: Viola
bullets: Comes forward for treats, mouthy when taking them, will lick a handler's hand
Flinches hard when touched on the body, flips her head away, freezes when she sees the leash
Pulled to sniff dogs through kennel fencing with a wagging tail, disengaged on her own
Jumped up on a seated handler, grabbed at the treat pouch with her mouth and pulled while grumbling, then turned and jumped high toward the handler's face while air snapping
A5169682.story: Viola is terrified and overstimulated in the shelter and her behavior is escalating under the pressure. She shows interest in people and other dogs, but her fear runs deep—she shuts down when startled, flinches when touched, and her arousal spikes into mouthing and snapping when she's overwhelmed. She has four days.
A5169682.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Viola needs an experienced handler who understands fear-based reactivity and can give her the structure and decompression time she has not had. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with behavior support resources by close of business August 19th.

A5169555.name: Wolfgang
bullets: Found as a stray after a scuffle with another dog; the person who found him brought him inside for the night and said he was friendly and calm once settled
In his evaluation, greeted the handler with a wagging tail, leaned into petting, rolled over for belly rubs, and sat for treats
Barked and postured at other dogs through the fence but disengaged quickly when redirected
Walked on leash with moderate pull, took treats gently, allowed full handling and petting
A5169555.story: Wolfgang is a tan and white Chihuahua mix who ended up at the shelter after being found loose. He's undersocialized with other dogs and can be reactive when startled or when things escalate quickly, but with a calm handler he softens fast. He's affectionate with people once he trusts the situation.
A5169555.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Wolfgang bit during a dog fight he ran into as a stray, and he needs an experienced handler in an adult-only home with no other dogs, someone who understands reactivity and won't put him in situations that set him up to fail. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by end of day August 19th.

A5168516.name: Suki
bullets: Gentle when taking treats from handlers after settling in, leans into people for affection and likes having her lower back scratched
Pulls hard on leash and reacts to other dogs—barked back and forth with small dogs, stared and pulled toward a large dog
Ran zoomies in the yard during intake, but has been too sick to eat for most of her shelter stay and is coughing up white foam
A5168516.story: Suki was found as a stray three weeks ago. She came in energetic and affectionate, the kind of dog who jumps up on the bench to press against you for more attention. But she has been battling chronic respiratory disease since arrival and has barely eaten. She has six days.
A5168516.needs: Suki is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of business August 24. She needs a home with no other dogs, experience with leash work and dog reactivity, and ideally older children only. She also needs someone ready to continue medical care for her respiratory condition.

A5170033.name: Yellowstone
bullets: Greets handlers at the kennel door with a low tail and neutral body, takes treats gently
Walks on leash, allows all handling and petting, solicits attention from people
Underweight with severe cardiac disease and multiple masses
A5170033.story: Yellowstone is an eight-year-old shepherd who still seeks out human company and takes treats gently despite being thin and very sick. He was found with another dog and brought in together. His body is failing him, but his trust in people has not wavered.
A5170033.needs: Yellowstone needs a partner rescue with the medical resources and hospice experience to give him comfort in whatever time he has left. He must be pulled by a registered New Hope Partner through the portal no later than 5:30 a.m. on August 21st.

A5169911.name: Big Mac
bullets: Walks slowly on leash through the shelter, hesitates at doorways and when passing people, needs gentle encouragement
In a quiet room, explored with his nose to the ground and approached a handler on his own to accept petting
Takes treats gently from a hand, but when alone in his kennel, chews on water bowls and metal fixtures
A5169911.story: Big Mac is a two-year-old Frenchie shutting down under the weight of shelter life. In his kennel he chews anything he can reach. Outside it, with a patient handler, he moves like someone trying to hold himself together. He'll come to you if you give him time, lift a paw and cry softly, let you touch him. But the fear is in every stiff step, every flinch, every moment he stands frozen by a fence unable to move.
A5169911.needs: Big Mac is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than August 23rd. He needs a quiet foster home with someone who understands fear this deep, who will not rush him, who can give him weeks to learn that the world is not this loud and this hard. This is not a beginner's dog.

A5169864.name: Chewy
bullets: Found as a stray, ran up to someone at a bus stop and allowed petting—friendly with strangers from the start.
Knows sit, walks on leash but pulls hard, takes treats (sometimes grabby, sometimes gentle).
Shows high arousal around other dogs—barking, whining, pulling hard, vocal and tense when passing kennels.
In the yard alone with handlers, explores calmly, allows petting all over, soft body and wagging tail.
Jumps up on people repeatedly and has mounted handlers during interactions, redirects with leash pressure or treats.
A5169864.story: Chewy is an 80-pound young dog who approached a stranger at a bus stop like they were old friends, and that openness is still there when he's with people one-on-one. But the shelter has become overwhelming for him—he's over-aroused, reactive to other dogs in kennels, and his impulse control is unraveling under stress.
A5169864.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Chewy needs an experienced handler who understands overstimulation and can work on boundaries, leash skills, and helping him settle. Because he is New Hope Only, he must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 23.

A5169646.name: Colt
bullets: Solicits attention from handlers, leans in for petting, sits and downs on cue, responds to his name
Plays with toys in the yard, walks on leash with a strong pull, ignores other dogs when passing kennels
Spins, barks, and jumps in his kennel—four days to deadline and the stress is eating him alive
A5169646.story: Colt is a two-year-old shepherd who was found as a stray with another dog. Outside his kennel, he's affectionate and engaged—he knows commands, he wants to be near you, he settles on the bench and asks for scratches. Inside it, he's unraveling. The clock is the enemy here.
A5169646.needs: Experienced handler who understands that a dog losing it in confinement is not the same dog who will decompress in a home with space, time, and routine. Needs leash work and a calm environment to show who he actually is. Deadline is August 23rd.

A5169836.name: Cookie Dough
bullets: Came in with five other dogs, all found together
In handling sessions, trembled and flinched away from touch, though would approach handlers to sniff and briefly stand near them
Startled easily by movements and sounds, carried in a towel when moved because he would not walk on leash
Marked walls and attempted to mark people when in evaluation rooms
Growled during intake vaccinations under restraint
A5169836.story: Cookie Dough is an 11-pound Chihuahua mix who came in scared and has stayed that way. He will approach a person to investigate, but recoils when they try to pet him. His body says he does not feel safe yet, and the shelter cannot give him the time he needs to learn that hands will not hurt him.
A5169836.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Cookie Dough needs someone who understands fear and will not take his flinching personally, who can let him set the pace, and who has no expectation that he will be a lap dog anytime soon. Because he is New Hope Only, he must be pulled by a registered rescue partner through the portal by 5:30 a.m. on August 24th.

A5120241.name: Elmer
bullets: Knows sit, spin, down, paw, and shake—practiced, treat-motivated, worked closely with someone before
Solicits attention from handlers in the yard, checks in, sits calmly beside them when exploration is done
Strong puller on leash, jumps up but redirects, took treats a little grabby
Alarm barks and charges kennel gate when stressed—behavior that vanishes outside the kennel
Came into the shelter with another dog in August, has been through this cycle once before in March 2025
A5120241.story: Elmer is a four-year-old shepherd who transforms the moment he leaves his kennel. Inside, the shelter breaks him—alarm barking, gate charging, the kind of unraveling that happens to trained dogs with no way out. Outside, he's the dog he actually is: engaged, responsive, affectionate, a worker looking for his person. He has four days.
A5120241.needs: Experienced handler who understands kennel stress is not character. Home with kids twelve and up, proper introductions to any family members, leash work, and time to decompress without pressure. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise.

A5167012.name: Fergie
bullets: Knows sit and paw, takes treats gently, comes when called
Settled at handler's feet in the play yard after exploring and rolling in a mud puddle
Pulled into West Shelter two months ago and the kennel stress is eating her alive
Runs the fence line barking when people walk past the yard, especially children
Wiggly and soft-bodied one-on-one with handlers who take their time
A5167012.story: Fergie is a two-year-old pit mix who knows some basics and seeks out affection when the world slows down. In the kennel she spins out—barking, jumping, unraveling—but in a quiet yard with someone patient she'll chase a toy, practice commands, and eventually lean in for petting. The shelter is breaking her and she has four days.
A5167012.needs: No children. Experienced handler who understands a dog coming off the ceiling needs weeks to decompress, not demands on day one. Active home with a fenced yard and the patience to let her remember who she is underneath all this. Must be pulled by close of business August 23.

A5167238.name: Kleo
bullets: Trapped after weeks wandering loose near 47th Ave and Thomas, brought in by a finder who kept her in the trap overnight because she was too frightened to approach
In the shelter yard she explored at a distance, ate a treat or two, showed mild interest in toys if thrown, but would not approach handlers when called
Walked on leash with volunteers but startled hard at loud dogs and pulled away, resisted going back to her kennel, growled low when someone reached for the leash at her neck
A5167238.story: Kleo is a two-year-old husky who spent weeks on the street before someone could trap her, and six weeks at East have not made the world feel safer. She is wary of fast movements, of hands coming toward her, of enclosed spaces. She has shown a flash of interest in a thrown toy and will sometimes take a treat, but trust is not something she offers easily.
A5167238.needs: Kleo needs an experienced handler who understands fear and will not rush her, and a rescue partner willing to give her the months of decompression and slow work she will need to find out who she is when she is not afraid. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 23rd.

A5168183.name: Leo
bullets: Wandered into Laveen mid-July, friendly with the neighbor kids who found him, played gently with a 10-year-old in the lobby
Loves toys—grabs them, shakes them hard, plays fetch—and will sit on cue for treats
Strong on leash, pulls hard toward other dogs with intense focus, becomes overstimulated in the shelter and escalates quickly when aroused
Has snapped at the leash when worked up, mouthed handlers' hands during petting, muzzle-punched when amped, all without making contact but showing he loses his brakes
Stopped eating kibble in his kennel, refused treats through the bars, stress mounting after five weeks inside
A5168183.story: Leo is a seven-year-old husky mix who came in easy and sweet from the reservation, but the kennel is breaking him. He's a high-energy dog who needs an outlet and he doesn't have one, so the arousal spirals and the behavior gets harder to read. Underneath the escalation is a dog who sat for treats in the yard and let kids pet him in the lobby.
A5168183.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Leo needs an experienced handler who understands overstimulation, can manage a strong puller, and won't be rattled when he loses his off-switch. Must be pulled by a New Hope partner rescue no later than August 23.

A5169742.name: Nilla
bullets: Freezes when approached, stays pancaked to the ground, won't move from the spot handlers place her
Eats treats when offered, allowed handlers to leash her and carry her with a blanket without resistance
Trembles and flinches when touched, but does not bite or attempt to escape when picked up
A5169742.story: Nilla is a small white dog shutting down under the weight of her fear. She will take a treat, she will let you carry her, but she cannot yet move toward you on her own.
A5169742.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Nilla needs an experienced foster who understands severe fear and will not expect her to be normal anytime soon. Must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of business August 23rd.

A5165944.name: Rose
bullets: Walked on leash with mild pulling, ignored other dogs in the hallways when passing their kennels
Played fetch in the yard with good energy, brought the ball back to handlers and dropped it to keep the game going
Solicited attention from handlers, opened up quickly after an initial timid approach, took treats gently
A5165944.story: Rose came back to the shelter after two months in a home that couldn't work through housetraining with a baby on the way. She's a young dog with play drive and affection to give, but she's here on a short clock because of an incident that happened before that adoption, when she broke a leash and went after another dog.
A5165944.needs: Rose needs a experienced handler who understands dog aggression and can manage it without wishful thinking. No other dogs, no public outings where she might encounter them. She must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by close of business August 23rd.

A5170234.name: Dog A5170234
bullets: Handlers were able to hold him and pet his head slowly once he was wrapped in a towel or blanket
Does not walk on leash, needs to be carried
Sits in the back corner of his kennel, not interested in treats or approaching people on his own
Tense and timid during handling but allows it without growling or biting
A5170234.story: This ten-year-old Chihuahua is shutting down hard. He has a perianal mass and three days left. He tolerates handling when it happens to him, but he is not reaching back.
A5170234.needs: A hospice-experienced or senior-dog foster who understands a geriatric dog in medical crisis may never come around, and will not take it personally. Must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than 5:30am on August 24th.

A5167762.name: Chrome
bullets: Found as a stray in early July, neutered, walked to someone who called him and jumped right into their car
Walked on leash, interested in other dogs in passing, whined at them in the lobby, sniffed well through fences during recent yard time
Got in the pool during yard assessments, took treats, solicited attention from handlers, lower energy and loose body when out of his kennel
Pulling hard on leash, especially toward dogs, and showing conflict during some dog greetings—neutral from behind, tense face to face
Kennel life is breaking him down: licking walls, hypersalivating, leaping with fixed focus, self-injury, blood in the kennel, can't be distracted from the stress behaviors when confined
A5167762.story: Chrome came in friendly and willing, the kind of dog who hops in a stranger's car when called. Two months in a concrete run has sent him into a spiral of anxiety so deep he's hurting himself. Outside the kennel he's still there—loose, interested, responsive—but inside it he's unraveling fast.
A5167762.needs: An experienced foster who understands what sustained kennel stress does to a dog and can give him weeks of quiet decompression, no pressure, and time to remember what safety feels like. This is not a beginner's dog. He needs leash work, careful dog introductions, and someone who won't mistake shutdown for calm or arousal for aggression while he finds his footing again.

A5169777.name: Courage
bullets: Came in with two other dogs—whatever happened, he didn't go through it alone.
In the play yard, surveyed on his own, then slowly approached the handler and nudged for pets, softened when scratched under the neck and chest.
Freezes when it's time to return to the kennel—struggled, thrashed when pressured, had to be transported back in a behavior taxi.
The fear is deep enough that movement through the shelter causes him to shut down, pancake flat, or refuse to move.
Takes time, soft talk, and patience to get a leash on—but once he trusts you for a moment, he accepts touch and even wags his tail briefly.
A5169777.story: Courage is a three-year-old pit bull mix carrying more fear than any dog should have to. He can soften, he can wag, he can ask for affection—but the terror of confinement and being moved against his will overtakes him, and he shuts down or fights the leash. He needs someone who understands that this kind of fear doesn't evaporate in days, and who has the skill to meet him where he is without force.
A5169777.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He needs an experienced foster who knows how to work with a frightened dog over the long haul, who won't rush him, and who can give him the months it will take to decompress. Courage is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by end of business August 24th.

A5169840.name: Gelato
bullets: Came in with five other dogs, stood calmly with his kennel mate and took treats, but once separated he froze in the middle of the kennel and wouldn't come forward
Trembles when alone with people, backs away from touch, will take treats from a hand but won't seek contact or stay close
Shuts down when he's scared—pulls away, cowers, goes stiff—but allows himself to be carried and leashed without fighting
A5169840.story: Gelato is a small cream-colored Chihuahua mix who relied on his pack to feel safe, and without them he doesn't know what to do. He's not aggressive, but he's deeply frightened of handling and human attention, and right now that fear runs the whole show.
A5169840.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Gelato needs a foster with fearful-dog experience who can give him time and space to learn that people won't hurt him. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of day August 24th.

A5157368.name: Kray
bullets: Lived indoors since puppyhood with two adults, knows sit and come, housetrained and crate trained
Owner says he's been fine with other dogs and calm around the household birds
In the shelter he's tense and conflicted—approaches handlers but flinches and lip-curls when touched, dodges the leash, pulled hard to get back to his kennel
A5157368.story: Kray came in because his owner's health failed. He's a young dog whose world just collapsed, and the shelter is overwhelming him. He's trying to be social but his body keeps saying no—skin crawling under a hand, stiff tail, hard stares when someone reaches. That's fear, not meanness, but it's fear that could tip.
A5157368.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Kray needs someone who can read a conflicted dog, move slowly, not push, and give him time to decompress without physical pressure. He is New Hope Only, which means a qualified partner rescue must pull him by close of business August 24th.

A5170005.name: Nala
bullets: Knows sit, come, and shake; house-trained and leash-trained, though pulls hard when anxious
Lived quietly with another dog for two years, played well together; described as mellow at home unless it's playtime
Very frightened in the shelter—won't take treats, avoids handlers, startles at sudden movement and sound, shuts down when approached
A5170005.story: Nala came in when a family member's illness made it impossible to keep her. At home she was gentle with kids, good with the household dog, and steady once she felt safe. The shelter has broken her—she is too scared to let anyone close.
A5170005.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Nala needs someone who has worked with fearful dogs, who will not rush her, and who understands that a dog this shut down will take months of patient, skilled work to trust again. She is New Hope Only, which means she must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 24.

A5097409.name: Palomo
bullets: Knows sit, down, stay, rollover, spin, and several other commands—he came in with a vocabulary
Lived with his family for over four years, spent time with young children, was friendly and playful with his adults
Shuts down hard under shelter stress—stands frozen, tucks into corners, won't take treats, watches from a distance with every muscle tight
Surrendered because he digs under gates and escapes, and also because he growled at strangers and at the other dogs in his home
Crate trained, housetrained, walks on leash though he pulls sometimes
A5097409.story: Palomo is a three-year-old who spent most of his life in one home, learning tricks and living alongside people he trusted. The shelter has made him profoundly afraid—he cowers, he won't engage, he growls when cornered because he sees no other option. Under that fear is a dog who knows commands, who lived inside and outside, who had a routine and people who taught him things.
A5097409.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Palomo needs someone who understands fear-based behavior, who will not push him, who has secure fencing because he is an escape artist, and who has no other dogs or cats. He is New Hope Only, which means a registered rescue partner must pull him by close of business August 24th.

A5127527.name: Penelope
bullets: Knows sit, stay, lay down, go to bed, crate, roll over, and dead
House-trained and crate-trained, reportedly calm indoors—lounges around, medium energy
Previously adopted from this same shelter in 2025, returned after four months when anxiety developed around children
A5127527.story: Penelope came back through intake in August after her adopters reported aggression toward the children in the home. The record shows she was friendly with the kids at first, then something shifted. She's house-trained, knows her commands, and the adults said she was very smart and listened well, but this is a dog whose anxiety went somewhere she couldn't come back from on her own.
A5127527.needs: No children. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Penelope is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with experience in behavioral support and a plan for management, evaluation, and placement in an adult-only home.

A5169814.name: Ponyo
bullets: Twelve-pound Jack Russell terrier mix who freezes when frightened, body trembling, pressed against the back wall of his kennel
Will eventually accept gentle touch from a patient handler, though his skin crawls and he stays tense throughout
Takes a long time to process what's happening around him—staff have carried him in a towel to give him space to decompress
Has not bitten, but turns his head toward hands when touched while frightened
In his worst moments, ignores even high-value treats and goes completely still
A5169814.story: Ponyo is a year-old terrier who came into the shelter already shut down by fear. He doesn't know yet that a hand reaching for him might mean something other than threat. What the shelter has seen is a dog who tolerates handling because he has no other choice, not because he trusts it, and that gap between tolerance and trust is where the work lives.
A5169814.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Ponyo needs an experienced foster who understands fear-based behavior, knows not to push, and has the time to let a terrified animal learn that the world might be safe. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with a confirmed foster home by end of business August 24th.

A5164863.name: Tesla
bullets: Stray who pushed open a wooden gate, got himself captured with food by a kind stranger who saw him friendly with another large dog in the home during that one day
Pulls hard on leash when he wants to investigate something, explored the yard with high energy, did play bows when handlers interacted with him
Shuts down in the kennel—went from soft and wiggly one day to erratically jumping, snapping at the leash, lunging and getting mouthy with handlers the next as the shelter days stacked up
Sat for treats during evaluations, allowed petting, yawned through the stress, walked back to his kennel without issue when calm
A5164863.story: Tesla has been at the shelter three months and the kennel is breaking him down. He came in as a stray who was good with another dog and easy in a home for the one day someone had him, but the concrete and noise have pushed him past what he can handle. What you're seeing now is not who he is.
A5164863.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Tesla needs an experienced handler who understands barrier frustration and kennel deterioration, a home with older kids only (12+), and proper decompression time to remember he's safe. He has four days.

A5167019.name: Vida
bullets: Likes other dogs—on walks, pulled toward every dog she could reach, touched noses, tail wagging, no growling, just wanted to say hello.
In the yard, paced at first, but came to handler several times, put her chin in their lap, closed her eyes when petted.
Resource guards her food bowl and kennel space—has lunged and snapped at hands near the opening, especially at feeding time.
A5167019.story: Vida is a three-year-old pit bull who loves other dogs and seeks out human contact when she feels safe. But three months in a concrete kennel has wound her tighter and tighter, and now she guards the small space she has left. She needs out before she breaks completely.
A5167019.needs: Must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 24. Experienced handler only. Someone who understands resource guarding and can give her the structure, space, and time to decompress. Not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise.

A5170210.name: Max
bullets: Lay quietly in his kennel when handlers approached, allowed petting
Walked on leash, accepted handling for vaccines without conflict
Showed some initial tension at intake but softened through the process
A5170210.story: Max is fourteen years old and came in stiff and uncertain. He has a heart murmur that puts him on medical priority. What handlers have seen since is a senior dog who settles, walks, and lets people work with him without a fight.
A5170210.needs: A quiet place with someone who understands older dogs and the medical care that comes with them. He has six days.

A5148378.name: Atlas
bullets: Greets visitors with loose body, tail wagging in circles, wiggling back and forth at the kennel gate, then sits.
Walks on leash with interest in other dogs at the park, takes treats gently, knows sit, down, stay, spin, and paw.
House-trained, crate-trained, loves car rides, seeks attention from people and plays well with other dogs.
A5148378.story: Atlas came back to the shelter a year after his first adoption because Valley Fever treatment costs became too much. His owner tried every resource offered and got denials across the board. He's the same playful, people-loving dog he was before, just carrying a diagnosis that needs consistent medication.
A5148378.needs: A home with no cats or small animals, and the financial cushion to manage ongoing Valley Fever treatment (fluconazole twice daily). Family introductions recommended.

A5168355.name: Camellia
bullets: Soft and wiggly when handlers approach, wagging tail and placing paws up to ask for attention without jumping or being pushy.
Gentle with people—crawls into laps for petting, gives kisses, leans in for affection.
Walks easily on leash, loose and stays close, alternates between drinking from the pool and coming back for more petting.
Has not been eating her kibble in the shelter, though she's alert and seeking contact with people.
Came in with another dog on July 15th and has been at West for over a month.
A5168355.story: Camellia is a 37-pound brindle girl who knows how to ask for what she wants—a soft lean, paws up, tail going. She's been at West for five weeks with a persistent respiratory issue that hasn't cleared, and she's barely touching her food. The clock is running.
A5168355.needs: A foster who can get her out of the shelter and into a quiet place to breathe, eat, and rest. She's flagged as a medical priority with seven days left, so we need someone now.

A5169863.name: Biscuit
bullets: Found in a park, allowed gentle handling from his finder and their young children
Knows sit, was kept indoors as a free-roaming house dog by the person who found him
In the shelter he shuts down—freezes in place, trembles, won't eat, defecates from fear
So frightened he tries to escape into adjacent kennels when handlers approach
Allows all physical handling without aggression even when terrified
A5169863.story: Biscuit is a thirteen-pound Maltese who came in gentle enough to sit with toddlers, and now he is so afraid in the shelter that he cannot move. He pancakes, he trembles, he turns his head away, and sometimes his body gives out entirely. This is what terror looks like in a small white dog who has never shown a moment of aggression but has run out of ability to cope.
A5169863.needs: Biscuit is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 25th. He needs an experienced foster who understands shutdown, can give him time and space without pressure, and will not mistake his frozenness for calm. This is not a beginner's dog.

A5166134.name: Dougie
bullets: Pulls hard on leash but walks willingly; knows sit and kennel
Soft and wiggly with handlers, leans in for pets, takes treats gently, rolls over for belly rubs
Friendly at the dog park—sniffs, tries to play, no aggression noted
Loves attention, mouthy during play, jumps up when excited
Returned to the shelter after two weeks because he chewed baseboards and walls, broke out of his crate, and wasn't housetrained
A5166134.story: Dougie is a young, affectionate dog with a high motor and a history that tells the truth: he cannot be left alone. His previous adopter brought him back after two weeks because the separation anxiety was more than they could handle. He needs someone who understands that this won't resolve in days or weeks, and who has the time, the setup, and the commitment to work through it.
A5166134.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Dougie needs a foster with separation anxiety experience, a plan for management and slow conditioning, and no expectation that he'll be housetrained or crate-comfortable anytime soon. New Hope Only—a partner rescue must pull him by end of business August 25.

A5169838.name: Jingle
bullets: Came in with five other dogs, found together
In the small yard, paced the fence with his tail tucked, then slowly laid across a handler's lap and let himself be petted
Startles easily and air-snapped once when someone reached too fast, but takes treats gently and wraps his paws around a handler's arm
Trembles through most handling but is beginning to show moments of relaxation
Flinches away from hands coming over his head
A5169838.story: Jingle is a fifteen-pound terrier shut down by fear. He came in with a group of dogs two weeks ago and the shelter is too much for him. Under the shaking, there is a dog who will lean into someone who moves slowly and speaks quietly.
A5169838.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Jingle needs an experienced foster who understands fear-based behavior and will not rush him. He must be pulled by a New Hope partner rescue by end of business August 25.

A5167708.name: Picasso
bullets: Came in as a stray with an ear wound and crusty eyes, found wandering 67th Avenue and Encanto
Walks on leash, explores calmly with his nose to the ground, accepts gentle petting
When aroused by treats or excitement, he bites at pouches, clothing, hands—fast enough to leave marks
Sits on cue, leans in for scratches, mostly soft and wiggly when not overstimulated
Struggles to regulate himself when he wants something, and shelter life is making it worse
A5167708.story: Picasso is a six-year-old brown pit bull who showed up alone in July with an injured ear. He knows how to walk nicely and take treats gently when he's calm, but when he gets worked up he loses his brakes—biting at treat bags, mouthing hands and clothes hard enough to leave marks, demand-barking and hopping. He's not mean. He's dysregulated, and the kennel is winding him tighter every day.
A5167708.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Picasso needs an experienced handler who understands arousal and can teach him to settle before he tips over the edge, in a quiet home without other animals or young children. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by close of business August 25th.

A5170060.name: Timmy
bullets: Lived inside for three years with his owner, housetrained, knows sit and stay, good on leash
Owner described him as friendly with kids and dogs at the park and visitors' dogs at home
Shuts down hard in the shelter: won't take treats, avoids handling, flinches when touched, keeps distance from people even in the yard
Ears pinned, tail tucked, lip licking, heavy panting when handlers approach or adjust his leash
Ducks away from leash placement, will not enter kennel on his own, maintains arm's length even when called
A5170060.story: Timmy spent three years in a home before life changes brought him here, and the shelter has broken something in him. He is terrified. The friendly dog his owner described is nowhere in sight right now, just a husky mix trying to disappear into himself.
A5170060.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Timmy needs an experienced foster who understands fear and will not rush him, in a calm home without chaos. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 25th.

A4510633.name: Patrick
bullets: Owned for 6 years, surrendered when family had young children and Patrick struggled with unpredictability around infants—lunged at a toddler once but never bit
Kennel-trained, potty-trained, knows sit/stay/shake, likes long walks and car rides, loves cuddles and chew toys with adults and older kids
Walked parallel with another shelter dog without issue, goes into zoomies in play yard, hesitant to return to kennel but allows being carried
Pulls on leash, walks best in a harness, ignores other dogs in kennels, takes treats nicely from handlers
Deadline August 27, listed as medical priority with 6 days left
A4510633.story: Patrick spent six years with one family before they surrendered him when they had babies and couldn't manage the risk. He's affectionate with older people, playful, trained, and house-mannered. He needs a home that understands what happened and won't put him in that position again.
A4510633.needs: Adults only or older children 12+, no young kids. Only dog in the home. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Patient handler who can work with leash pulling and give him the structure he's used to.

A5170274.name: Dog A5170274
bullets: Takes hotdogs gently from a handler's hand through the kennel door, then stares at the empty bag and moans softly when they're gone.
Retreats to the back of her kennel when approached, but comes forward to sniff hands and check for more treats.
Walks on leash, allows handling and petting, soft body when touched, tucks her tail.
A5170274.story: She's three years old, thirty-seven pounds, and so shut down with fear that she won't leave her bed even when the door opens. She has an ulcerated mass on her leg that needs treatment now.
A5170274.needs: Medical foster who can give her time to decompress and get her leg treated. New Hope Only, so she must be pulled by a partner rescue before end of business August 24th.

A5170118.name: Acorn
bullets: Shuts down hard in the kennel—backs into corners, trembles, won't take treats, watches handlers with whale-eyed stares
Extremely reactive to noise and movement, especially passing barking dogs—freezes, scurries, darts away with tail tucked
In quieter spaces, briefly explored a yard and hid under chairs near a handler, eventually eating a dropped treat
Walks on leash with light pull once out of the kennel building, can be directed, allowed handlers to slowly approach and secure leash
Took a jackpot of treats off the kennel floor when left alone
A5170118.story: Acorn is a 25-pound pit mix so afraid in the shelter that she becomes a statue. She backs into corners, stares hard, shakes. But the notes show flickers—she explored a yard for a moment, she inched closer to a handler who stayed still, she ate a treat when the pressure lifted. She is very young and very small and very scared, and what she does when the world stops closing in on her is still unknown.
A5170118.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Acorn needs someone who understands deep fear, who will not rush her, and who can give her the months of quiet and patience it will take to find out who she is underneath the shutdown. She must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by close of business August 26.

A5169984.name: Colton
bullets: When handlers crouch low and speak softly, Colton wags his tail, licks hands, accepts treats gently, and leans into petting.
Crawled into a handler's lap, put his head on their legs, lay down at their feet.
Freezes, cries out, and bites at the leash when anyone tries to put it on—handlers now use a lassoed loop and position themselves as barriers while coaxing him into a transport taxi instead.
Flinches hard at sudden sounds and movements, but softens when given time and space.
Once the leash is on and he's in the yard, he approaches people on his own, hops up to say hello, and sits close.
A5169984.story: Colton is a cattle dog who wants contact—he leans, he licks, he crawls forward for more petting—but something about the leash terrifies him. Handlers have learned to work around it by crouching, talking gently, giving him time, and letting him choose to move toward them. Underneath the fear is a dog who seeks out laps and affection.
A5169984.needs: Colton needs an experienced foster who understands fearful dogs and won't rush him, who can work with a trainer on leash desensitization, and who has the patience to let him set the pace. This is not a beginner's dog. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of day August 26th.

A5168987.name: Karma
bullets: Knows sit and go-to-bed, lived inside for four years, house-trained and alerts at the door when she needs to go out
Lived with three adults and three young children, played with some of the dogs in her household
Startles badly when approached fast or caught off guard and will bark, shuts down hard under kennel stress
A5168987.story: Karma came in when her family lost their housing. The kennel has been brutal for her. Early notes show a dog who played and took treats nicely. Three weeks in, she's barking at gate approach, hard staring, lunging. This is what fear looks like when it has nowhere to go.
A5168987.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Needs someone who understands a dog reacting from a place of being trapped, who will not approach fast or startle her, and who has the skill to help her remember who she was before this. New Hope Only, so a partner rescue must pull by close of business August 26.

A5170251.name: Logo
bullets: Was friendly with a visiting three-year-old and lived with two pit bulls he played with daily for two and a half years
In the shelter he shuts down hard—pancakes to the floor, trembles, won't walk on leash, flinches when touched, thrashes when handlers try to move him
Once outside in the yard he explored with his nose to the ground and rested his head in a handler's lap while being petted
Chases cats
Not housetrained, not leash trained, doesn't know commands—his owner said he needs training but didn't have the tools to provide it
A5170251.story: Logo is an eighty-nine-pound bulldog mix whose owner surrendered him when entering a nursing home. He lived outside for two and a half years with dogs he liked and a child he was gentle with, but he never learned to walk on a leash or come when called. The shelter terrifies him so completely that he goes rigid and shakes, which makes it nearly impossible to see who he actually is.
A5170251.needs: Logo is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a partner rescue with experience bringing a fear-shutdown dog back to himself. No cats. Deadline is August 26th.

A5167017.name: Madden
bullets: Volunteers describe him as playful, affectionate, gentle with treats, a fetch enthusiast who flings toys around and drops them at your feet for another round
Knows sit, leans in for petting, gives soft kisses, walked well on leash with handlers and sat calmly through meetings with strangers
Went home from MCACC once before—came back in one day after breaking a door to get at the household dog and drawing blood
A5167017.story: Madden is friendly, treat-motivated, and genuinely gentle with people. He is also intensely reactive to other dogs—barking, lunging, fence fighting, and willing to go through barriers to reach them. He needs someone who sees both those things clearly and has the skill to manage the second without losing sight of the first.
A5167017.needs: Only dog household, no exceptions. Experienced handler who has worked with serious dog aggression and understands the management and liability that come with it. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. New Hope Only—must be pulled by a partner rescue by August 26.

A5170097.name: Tommy
bullets: Found wandering near a dumpster four days before intake, skittish but allowed petting once coaxed with food
Knows sit and come, takes treats gently, appeared potty trained during his brief time with the finder
In the shelter: freezing, growling, lunging, defecating from fear when handlers approach—shutting down hard under the pressure of kennel life
A5170097.story: Tommy walked up for a hot dog and let a stranger pet him. Four days later he landed in a shelter kennel, and the fear kicked in so fast and so deep he can barely function. What handlers are seeing is a small dog in total system overload, trapped with no way out and no ability to reset.
A5170097.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Tommy needs an experienced, patient foster who understands fear-based reactivity and can give him the time and space to decompress outside of a kennel environment. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a partner rescue with the resources to support his rehabilitation. Deadline is August 26.

A5170369.name: Cookie
bullets: Found as a stray and spent a week with a finder who kept her crated inside, walked her on leash outside, and saw her ignore three cats completely
The finder's own dog barked and snapped at her, but Cookie never escalated back
Shelter handlers describe her as nervous and stiff in kennel, not seeking attention but allowing all handling and petting, lying calm while she slowly chewed dropped hot dogs
A5170369.story: Cookie is fifteen years old and was picked up as a stray with severe dental disease and a significant heart murmur. She is small and quiet and careful, the kind of dog who has learned to take up very little space in the world.
A5170369.needs: Cookie needs a foster who understands senior dogs with medical issues and can get her to a vet for assessment and ongoing care. She has eight days.

A5170374.name: Dog A5170374
bullets: A ten-year-old man who showed up at a worksite on Van Buren, greeted strangers with a wagging tail, took treats from handlers at intake
Walks slowly, curious, sniffs the ground; stretched and settled on his kennel bed
Cloudy eyes, overweight, hair loss on his elbows, resists leash pressure but doesn't bolt
A5170374.story: He walked in like he'd been walking a long time. Old, heavy on his feet, eyes clouded, but still friendly enough to greet the people who found him. Nobody came looking. He's ten, medically fragile, and running out of time.
A5170374.needs: A quiet adult home with someone who understands senior dogs and veterinary expense. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue no later than the morning of August 31.

A4921617.name: Max
bullets: Fourteen-year-old corgi mix who walked on leash and allowed petting and handling when staff worked with him
Lay quietly in his kennel, soft body during exam, though he showed some nervousness and didn't take treats
Nineteen pounds, white and black, senior dog with a heart murmur noted in his medical record
A4921617.story: Max is an elderly corgi mix who ended up at the shelter at fourteen years old. He's gentle with people and cooperated with everything handlers asked of him, though the stress shows—he's stiff, quiet, and won't eat treats in the kennel.
A4921617.needs: Max needs a partner rescue to pull him by end of business August 26th. He needs a home that understands senior dogs with medical needs, can go slow with introductions, and can give him the quiet decompression time an old dog in a shelter deserves.

A5165899.name: Mayor West
bullets: Found as a stray and spent one night with a finder who reported he was friendly with people, energetic, and jumped up for attention.
Pulls hard on leash and reacted to other dogs while walking, barking and pulling toward them.
In the shelter yard, explored on his own, stood near handlers but did not seek attention, allowed petting, and took treats gently.
Repeatedly reacted when staff walked past his kennel with other dogs—hackles raised, alarm barking, running the fence line.
Has upper airway disease that needs treatment.
A5165899.story: Mayor West came in as a stray with no known history. He is friendly and energetic with people but shows clear reactivity to other dogs—barking, pulling, raised hackles. In the yard he was more independent than social, checking in occasionally but mostly doing his own thing. He needs medical care for an upper airway condition.
A5165899.needs: Only dog. No young children. Someone with experience managing leash reactivity and who understands that this will take time and training work. Mayor West is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of business August 27.

A5170455.name: Dog A5170455
bullets: Found as a stray with severe skin disease and hair loss across her body, but still gentle enough to allow petting from a seven-year-old.
Walks well on leash, calm and quiet in the kennel, takes treats gently, allowed all handling at intake.
Lived one day with a finder who reported she was dismissive of the other dog in the home but not aggressive, ate her food fast while watching the other dog.
Staff saw her relaxed at the front of her kennel, tail tucked at intake but allowing touch and care.
A5170455.story: This three-year-old pit bull mix came in as a stray with extensive skin disease that will need dedicated treatment. Underneath the medical crisis is a dog who has stayed gentle and quiet through all of it.
A5170455.needs: A New Hope Partner rescue must pull her by end of business August 31st. She needs a foster prepared to manage ongoing skin treatment and a home that can go slow with a dog recovering her health and her confidence.

A4112190.name: Samson
bullets: Knows sit and shake, takes treats (sometimes grabby), walks on leash with some pull
Plays fetch and carries toys around the yard with a wagging tail
Seeks attention, solicits petting, allowed all handling from volunteers
Calm around other dogs when walking past kennels
Eleven years old, house-trained when kept inside, seventy-three pounds
A4112190.story: Samson has been bouncing between owners and back to the shelter since May. He's an eleven-year-old who still plays like he's got years ahead of him—fetching, goofing around with toys, wagging through it all. There was a dog fight in a front yard during one brief placement, and the shelter recommends he be the only dog.
A4112190.needs: A home where he can be the only dog, with someone who has the time to actually keep him. He has six days left and is listed as a medical priority.

A5169314.name: Autumn
bullets: Stays frozen on her bed when handlers approach, won't come forward even for treats, though she'll eat them if they're tossed to her
Once coaxed out to a yard, she explored briefly with a soft body and low wagging tail, then chose to lie down close to the handler and allowed petting
Skin crawls when first touched but she settles, eyes going soft, and she looks up when the petting stops
A5169314.story: Autumn is a five-year-old pit bull who shuts down hard in her kennel—frozen, won't move, retreats to the back when anyone comes near. But in a quieter space, with time and patience, she's shown she can soften: exploring on her own terms, sitting beside a handler, relaxing under gentle touch. She's been at the shelter nearly a month and the stress is deepening.
A5169314.needs: Autumn needs an experienced foster who understands shutdown fear and won't rush her, because this is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than close of business August 30th.

A5167071.name: Brom
bullets: Shy and tentative when handlers first approach, but warms enough to accept pets and take treats gently
Walks on leash with handlers, though sometimes hesitant, stopping and needing soft encouragement to keep going
Easily startled by sudden movements and sounds, goes high-alert in response to noise
Has grabbed the leash during handling, once catching a handler's finger hard enough to break skin
Ignores most dogs when walking past kennels but barks at the fence when dogs or people pass the yard
A5167071.story: Brom is a four-year-old pit bull who came in timid and has stayed that way, a dog who startles easily and shuts partway down under stress. He has moments of warmth with patient handlers but the shelter environment has pushed him past his threshold, and his anxiety has escalated into redirected biting on the leash. He needs out.
A5167071.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Brom needs an experienced foster with a New Hope rescue partner who understands fearful dogs, can give him space and time to decompress, and knows how to read and work with a dog who bites when overwhelmed. Must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by close of business August 30th.

A5169546.name: Domo
bullets: Shuts down hard in the kennel—lies in the back, trembling, won't take treats, averts his gaze, whale-eyed with ears pinned.
Won't walk on leash but will load himself into a behavior taxi if it's placed close enough.
In the yard, slowly exited the taxi after several minutes, sniffed nearby, urinated, stood near a handler on a bench.
Handlers have been able to leash him and move him for cleaning, but he tenses when approached and makes chuffing sounds when people get close.
Fear is so deep he has to be muzzle-wrapped and lifted to move him some days.
A5169546.story: Domo is a two-year-old pit bull mix who has been at the shelter three weeks and the fear has swallowed him whole. He shakes, he won't eat, he won't walk, he barely moves. In the yard he has shown a few flickers—sniffing, standing near a person—but inside the kennel he is frozen. This is a dog who needs someone who understands that fear this extreme is not something you love away in a weekend.
A5169546.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Domo needs an experienced foster with a quiet home, no expectations, and the patience to let him decompress for as long as it takes. He is New Hope Only, which means a qualified rescue partner must pull him by end of day August 30th.

A5170140.name: Guido
bullets: Approached handler with soft body and wagging tail, demand barking, easy to leash
In the play yard stayed near handlers most of the time, brief tail wag, grabbed treats when offered, chased tennis balls then lost interest
Pulls hard on leash, flinches when startled or when leash first makes contact, then settles
Stiffens when neighboring dogs bark, appears cautious inside the building but walks with more confidence once familiar with the route
A5170140.story: Guido is a young Malinois mix trying to find his footing in a world that startles him. He seeks nearness to people but doesn't quite know what to do with it yet—he'll stand close, brush against you, watch your face. There's a bite on record from play that got too rough, and he shuts down hard under pressure.
A5170140.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Guido needs a Malinois-experienced foster who understands fear, arousal, and a dog still learning his own body and boundaries. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 30th.

A5169757.name: Lemonade
bullets: Fence fights hard with other dogs, lunging and muzzle punching at kennels, leaping high at fences, losing focus on everything else when another dog is near
In the yard away from other dogs, chased a tennis ball, carried a toy around, demonstrated sit, took treats from handlers
Requires firm leash pressure to redirect past neighboring dogs and kennels, pulls hard, becomes very vocal
A5169757.story: Lemonade is a two-year-old pit mix whose world narrows to a single point when she sees another dog. The shelter has pushed her reactivity past what they can work with, and what handlers are seeing now is a dog wound tight and fixated.
A5169757.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Lemonade needs an experienced handler who understands serious dog reactivity and can manage a dog who fence fights, pulls hard on leash, and loses the ability to take direction when another dog is in range. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by end of business August 30th.

A5170202.name: Randall
bullets: Froze when approached, lifted a paw and showed whale eye when a handler reached toward him, stayed tense through handling but did not bite or snap
Allowed handlers to drape a towel over him, carry him, and slip leashes on and off while he stayed rigid and still
Urinated and defecated in the yard, may have been housetrained before this
Spent most of yard time sitting motionless under a tree or near the gate, watching, not engaging
Finder reported he was friendly with large and small dogs, a calm lap dog once he warmed up, tried to bolt out the front door when startled
A5170202.story: Randall is a 12-pound Shih Tzu who appears to have shut down completely in the shelter. He tolerates handling without aggression, but he is profoundly scared—frozen in place, barely moving, not eating treats, staring with wide eyes. The person who found him said he needed patience to warm up, that he was friendly and calm once he felt safe. Right now he does not feel safe.
A5170202.needs: Randall needs a quiet adult home with someone who has fostered or owned a deeply fearful dog before, who will not rush him, who understands that progress is measured in weeks, not days. This is not a beginner's dog. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 30th.

A5157016.name: Spruce
bullets: Leans into handlers for pets and attention, soft body and wagging tail when people approach
Knows sit, takes treats gently, house-trained and crate-trained
Pulls hard on leash when excited, lunges and vocalizes when dogs walk past
Shuts down in the kennel and has started hurting herself from the stress
A foster wrote that she slept most of the day, took her medicine without fuss, never barked once, and went to her bed when told no
A5157016.story: Spruce was adopted in January, surrendered in May when her person lost housing, placed informally with an older couple, and brought to the shelter in August when that arrangement ended. She has been at the West Shelter for a week and the kennel environment is breaking her down. Outside the kennel she is the dog the foster described: calm, affectionate, eager to please, a leaner.
A5157016.needs: Spruce needs out by close of business August 30. She needs a quiet adult home with no other dogs, someone who understands that a dog losing her mind in a kennel is not the same dog who will decompress in yours, and the patience to let her sleep for days when she gets there. Requires very slow introductions to other dogs and may do best as an only.

A5170136.name: Miriam
bullets: Twelve-year-old shepherd who walks with a handler who talks softly and lets her set the pace.
Explored the yard, nose to ground, approached when called, sat in the shade and accepted petting.
Took treats, some with eagerness, some a little grabby, let a handler wipe the gunk from her eyes.
A5170136.story: Miriam is a senior dog with a soft body and low tail wags, the kind of old girl who needs a minute to trust that you mean well. She froze once on leash when the world felt too big, then settled when given time. She has multiple medical issues that will need care and monitoring.
A5170136.needs: A quiet foster home with someone experienced enough to read an elderly dog's signals and give her the space and time she asks for. This is New Hope Only—she must be pulled by a partner rescue with medical support in place.

A5170527.name: Dog A5170527
bullets: Walked onto the ramp with handlers, took vaccines calmly, walks on leash at her own slow pace
Came to the front of her kennel to say hello with a relaxed body
Let male and female handlers pet her and handle her without worry
A5170527.story: She's a seven-year-old, five-pound senior with a body that's starting to show its age and medical needs the shelter can't meet long-term. She's still gentle with people, still interested in connection, but she's running out of time in a place built for younger, healthier dogs.
A5170527.needs: A quiet foster home experienced with senior dogs and willing to work with a rescue on her medical care. She is New Hope Only, which means a partner rescue must commit to pull her—she cannot go directly to a foster. This is not a beginner's dog.

A5170534.name: Dog A5170534
bullets: Found as a stray with another dog; the finder reported he was friendly with five large-breed dogs
Growled and tried to bite when handlers approached his face in intake, but has since greeted handlers calmly and allowed petting
Has a heart murmur and possible eye condition that will need veterinary attention
A5170534.story: This thirteen-pound Shih Tzu mix came in scared and defensive, snapping when people reached toward his face. Since then he has softened—greeting handlers with a calm body, allowing touch. He was found with another dog and the finder said he did well with a pack of large dogs, so there is a steadier dog under the fear.
A5170534.needs: A quiet adult home with someone who understands a small dog who has learned to use his teeth when cornered is not a bad dog, just a frightened one. No quick movements near his face until trust is built. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a registered partner rescue. He has six days.

A5168496.name: Phoebe
bullets: Jumped willingly into a stranger's car when she was found loose and wandering, allowed a five-year-old to climb on her and handle her completely
Knows sit, down, and stay; walks loose leash; takes treats gently and comes over for petting when she's ready
Watched the finder's cat closely with focus but no aggression; played fine with a small dog but barked excitedly at a large dog through the fence
Timid and slow to warm in the shelter but softens once she trusts you—handlers say she'll blossom with time
Marked priority medical with three days left and requires a New Hope partner rescue to pull her
A5168496.story: Phoebe was picked up wandering near a Peoria convenience store and jumped right into a car with a stranger, sweet and willing from the start. She's been gentle and calm through a month in the shelter, though the stress shows—she's quiet, a little sad, slow to eat, and needs reassurance when things get loud. Under the worry is a dog who knows commands, walks beautifully on leash, and leans into the people who give her time.
A5168496.needs: She needs a foster home with no cats, older or no kids, and a slow introduction to the routine—someone who understands a dog can be both gentle and unsure, and won't rush her. This is a New Hope Only pull, which means she must be selected by a registered rescue partner through the portal no later than 5:30 a.m. on August 31st and picked up within 24 hours.

A5170132.name: Amadeus
bullets: Knows sit and down, will demonstrate both on cue and lean into touch once he settles
Jumps repeatedly when excited—at doors, at people, at the leash—then gradually calms enough to redirect with treats
Chases thrown toys for a few tosses, then loses interest and wanders off to sniff
Mouths gently at hands when petted, stopped after a few minutes and relaxed next to handler on the bench
Gets overaroused quickly in transitions—kennel to yard, yard to kennel—demand barks and jumps at the leash
A5170132.story: Amadeus is a young Malinois-type dog with a ton of energy and very little impulse control. He knows some commands and wants to engage, but he cycles between frantic arousal and brief pockets of calm, and right now he has no way to manage himself in between. He's been too much dog for the shelter to handle safely.
A5170132.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Amadeus needs an experienced handler who understands high-drive working breeds, can manage arousal and mouthing, and has the time and skill to teach him how to exist in the world without spinning out. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with behavior support resources by end of day August 31st.

A5170125.name: Bear
bullets: Walked on leash with moderate pull, marked and defecated in yard
Soft wiggly body, sought out petting and human attention from handlers, took treats gently
Became fixated on tennis ball in play yard, retrieved it repeatedly to handlers
Knows sit and stay, house-trained, lived both inside and outside
Growled at other dogs while being walked to kennels
A5170125.story: Bear is a high-energy two-year-old who has lived in two homes in the past year and has not been neutered or vaccinated. He redirected and bit his teenage owner's hand when the owner intervened during an attack on the family's cat. The cat did not survive.
A5170125.needs: Bear killed a cat and has bitten a person. He is not safe with cats, shows tension around other dogs, and has high energy that has never been channeled through training or structure. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Bear is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with the capacity to manage a dog with this bite history by August 31st.

A5170144.name: Biscotti
bullets: Found crossing the street, barking at strangers, warmed up when offered treats
In the yard, ran zoomies, rolled over for petting, jumped up when over-aroused but responded to correction
Tenses and flags when he sees other dogs, barks and growls at small dogs
Refuses to go back into the kennel, pulls back hard, goes wide-eyed and rigid, requires physical guidance to get him inside
A5170144.story: Biscotti has been in a shelter kennel for nine days and he is unraveling. Somebody found him loose and brought him in. He can be sweet and wiggly with handlers in the yard, but the kennel itself terrifies him now, and the resistance is escalating. He needs out.
A5170144.needs: Must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 31. Biscotti is reactive to strangers and to small dogs, and he shuts down or freezes under pressure. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He needs an experienced handler who understands fear and can give him the structure and space to decompress outside of concrete and chain link.

A5170362.name: Chino
bullets: Lived outside for four or five years, no leash experience, no dog contact, no child contact, owner said he'd bark but allow handling
In the shelter, freezes completely when asked to walk, flinches hard from touch, trembles, jumps at doors trying to get out
Will take treats gently from a still hand, but keeps his distance and his skin crawls when petted
Carried in a blanket wrap because he won't move on leash, flailed once when picked up, otherwise goes tense and still
Staff noted periodic coughing and a history of reacting to loud noises by hiding or barking
A5170362.story: Chino spent years in a backyard with almost no handling, and now the world inside four walls is more than he can bear. He shuts down hard under pressure, and what looks like compliance is actually a dog too scared to move.
A5170362.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He needs someone who understands fear this deep, who won't push, who has the time and skill to let a dog like this find his own way back. New Hope Only, so he must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 31.

A5170205.name: Elijah
bullets: Walked right up to a stranger on the street three years into his life and decided they were his person for the next three days.
Spent those days living alongside three dogs and a cat without incident, knew how to walk on leash, settled in a crate but preferred to be out with people.
In the shelter he alarm barks at kennel approach, air snaps when over threshold, and pulls hard on leash—staff notes high arousal and difficulty managing him safely in this environment.
A5170205.story: Elijah is a 50-pound bull terrier mix who appeared out of nowhere near 43rd and Bethany Home, friendly enough that someone took him in for three days before bringing him here. In a home he was calm around people and animals. In the shelter he is falling apart.
A5170205.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Elijah needs a foster with bull terrier or high-arousal-dog experience who understands that what the shelter is seeing is fear and overwhelm, not who he is. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than August 31.

A5170158.name: Kalani
bullets: Kalani shuts down hard when handlers approach—pancakes flat, trembles, won't take treats even when afraid.
Once outside she follows on leash, tolerates gentle touch, will settle at your feet and let you sit quietly with her.
Hyper-alert to everything passing by—other dogs, sounds, movement—then bolts for gates or pulls toward exits, trying to find a way out.
After each wave of fear she comes back, lies down next to the handler again, lets them stroke her while she shakes.
A5170158.story: Kalani is a three-year-old shepherd mix drowning in fear at the shelter. She doesn't bite, doesn't bark, doesn't fight—she just folds into herself and tries to disappear. When the world gets quiet she softens a little, leans in, shows you the dog underneath all that terror.
A5170158.needs: Kalani needs an experienced foster who understands shutdown fear and won't rush her, and a home with no other dogs while she learns the world isn't going to hurt her. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of business August 31st.

A5170230.name: Mortimer
bullets: Came in with another dog, both surrendered together on August 19th
Freezes when woken, trembles hard, won't make eye contact
Panics when lifted or leashed—thrashes, cries out, hyperventilates, has urinated from fear
Shuts down in new spaces, tucks himself into corners with his head turned away
Allows some gentle head scratches when he's too frozen to move
A5170230.story: Mortimer is an eight-year-old Chihuahua who is so terrified in the shelter he can barely function. He doesn't know how to be handled by strangers, and the concrete and fluorescent lights have pushed him past his limit. This is a dog who needs the world to slow down and someone who knows that trust is built in silence, not coaxing.
A5170230.needs: Mortimer needs an experienced foster who has worked with shut-down, fear-reactive dogs and understands that progress is measured in weeks, not days. This is not a beginner's dog. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than August 31st.

A5163733.name: Rocket
bullets: Calm in a busy shelter—when handlers walked past his yard or cleaned kennels around him while other dogs barked, he wagged and watched, unbothered.
Warmed up quickly once given space to settle—timid at first if approached too fast or loomed over, but with slow movement he relaxed and stood near his handler.
Walked on leash with mild pull, ignored passing dogs in the hallway, sniffed around the yard and came when called.
Has a history of resource guarding people—lunged and bit someone who walked away from his previous owner, leaving a bruise.
Reactive to movement—chases cats, rabbits, birds, and barks or growls at strangers until he knows them.
A5163733.story: Rocket is an 8-year-old Min Pinscher mix who spent two months in a home before his owner surrendered him after the bite incident. In the shelter he has been steady and responsive with handlers who move slowly and let him come to them, but his history shows he can escalate when someone he is guarding leaves or when he feels uncertain about a stranger.
A5163733.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Rocket needs an experienced handler who understands resource guarding and can manage his reactivity to small animals and strangers. No cats, no children, a secure home with predictable routines. Rocket is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with the capacity to support his behavior long-term.

A5165599.name: Zane
bullets: Jumped up on handlers, wrapping front paws around them and pushing off—a hard, physical greeting that happened repeatedly
Walked with a strong pull on leash, paced fence lines with tail up and heavy panting, could not settle even with treats
Played independently with toys and tennis balls in the yard, carrying them around and shaking them in the air
Reacted intensely when seeing other dogs through the fence, rushing the fence line and trying to jump up
Showed increasing over-arousal in the shelter setting, making safe handling more difficult over time
A5165599.story: Zane is a 67-pound three-year-old who has big energy and no off switch in the kennel environment. He plays hard, greets harder, and the stress of shelter life is winding him tighter every day. He needs out now, into a home that can give him structure, space to decompress, and a handler who won't be knocked off balance—literally or otherwise.
A5165599.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Zane needs an experienced handler in a calm, structured home with no other dogs, someone who can manage a strong dog with impulse control issues and give him the time and training to settle. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with behavioral support resources by August 31.

A5169620.name: Amarillo
bullets: 90-pound shepherd who came in with two other dogs in early August
Can be leashed outside his kennel with patience and food, then pulls hard past the behavior taxi
Struggles with leash handling—bites and thrashes at the leash, alligator rolls, redirects onto handler's clothing when frustrated
On good days walked softly in the yard, independently but affiliatively, and went back into his kennel with gentle steering
A5169620.story: Amarillo is a big shepherd caught between two versions of himself. When the pressure drops and someone moves slowly, he softens—takes treats, allows leashing, even opts to go back inside his kennel on his own. But the kennel environment is eroding him fast, and his frustration now floods over into biting at the leash, thrashing, and redirecting onto handlers when he can't cope. He has five days left and the shelter has named him New Hope Only because he is becoming unsafe to move.
A5169620.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Amarillo needs an experienced foster or adopter who understands fearful, frustrated shepherds and can give him the structure, space, and time to decompress outside of concrete and noise. Must be pulled by a qualified New Hope Partner rescue no later than close of business September 1st.

A5169824.name: Athena
bullets: Returned after one week because she made contact with a 4-year-old who tried to pet her—no skin broken—and air-snapped when people tried to pick her up
Found miles from home with bloody paws after running, shut down hard in the shelter and lay flat on her side through an entire vaccine appointment without moving
Knows sit and paw, leaned into handlers for affection in the yard, rolled over for belly rubs, walked well on leash once on her feet
A5169824.story: Athena is a 91-pound dog whose fear looks like shutdown, not noise. She went from rolling for belly rubs in the yard to lying motionless through handling, which tells you how deep the stress runs. She set a boundary with a small child who kept trying and air-snapped when grabbed, both of which are communication, not aggression, but both of which mean she needs space and people who understand pressure.
A5169824.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Athena needs an adult-only home with someone who reads dogs well, moves slowly, and doesn't crowd or grab. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with behavior support by close of business September 1st.

A5170112.name: Butterfly
bullets: Shuts down hard when afraid: freezes in place, won't take treats, presses into walls with legs pinned under her.
Handling terrifies her. Thrashed under a towel, leapt from a kennel to escape being touched, went rigid when picked up.
In a quiet room alone she explored a little, jumped onto a bench, laid down—but the second a handler got close she locked up again.
A5170112.story: Butterfly came in with two other dogs, likely a backyard situation that fell apart. She is small and deeply frightened, the kind of scared that makes her bolt or freeze depending on whether she has an exit. Under all that fear there may be a dog who can learn to trust, but right now she cannot tolerate being handled and the shelter is too much for her.
A5170112.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Butterfly needs an experienced foster with a quiet home, no kids, someone who understands fearful dogs and won't rush her. She must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by close of business September 1st.

A5170247.name: Fozzy
bullets: Found as a stray, stayed briefly with a finder who saw him free-roam calmly with an 11-year-old, a 16-year-old, young puppies, and cats.
At the shelter he shuts down hard—trembling in the corner, whale-eyed, uninterested in treats, startled by noise and movement in the building.
In the yard with one calm handler he softens: approaches, rests his head in a lap, allows petting, checks in, gives slow tail wags.
Easily startled when leashed near reactive dogs or when staff walk past, pulls away with ears back and body low, but responds to verbal coaxing and continues.
A5170247.story: Fozzy is a two-year-old brindle and white dog who seemed to handle home life fine before he ended up on the streets. The shelter terrifies him. He freezes, he trembles, he watches everything like it might hurt him. But when a handler sits still in the yard and lets him come close on his own terms, he leans in.
A5170247.needs: Fozzy needs an experienced, patient foster who understands fear and won't rush him, in a quiet home without chaotic energy or reactive dogs. This is not a beginner's dog. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business September 1st.

A5170421.name: Grizzly
bullets: Came into the shelter with a wagging tail, let staff pet him and scan for a chip
Knew sit, crate trained, slept in his crate at night, housebroken
In the shelter became fearful—tensed up, whale-eyed, and flipped his head toward hands when startled by touch
Raised hackles and barked at small dogs through the fence
Paced the yard with wide eyes and a tucked tail, easily startled by loud noises
A5170421.story: Grizzly came in as a friendly puppy who knew basic commands and had good house manners. The shelter has broken him. He is now a dog who growls when approached in his kennel, flinches hard at sounds, and cannot settle.
A5170421.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Grizzly needs an experienced handler who understands fear and can give him the time and space to learn that the world is not always this frightening. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business September 1st.

A5170246.name: Ms Silly
bullets: Finder reported she was good with an 11-year-old, a 16-year-old, young puppies, and cats during the few days they had her
At the shelter she pancakes to the back of her kennel, trembles, and has lunged with air snaps when handlers kneel down
Once outside she follows handlers around, leans in for attention, and jumps up for pets with a soft body, but flinches hard when startled by sudden movement or sound
Will approach when called and soften after freezing, but tenses up again when touched on the body
A5170246.story: Ms Silly was found running scared in the streets and brought to a finder who reported no problems, but the shelter terrifies her.
