She shuts down hard in her kennel and has shown alarm barking, air snapping, and body language that says she is overwhelmed past what she can handle. Outside the kennel she wants connection and will seek out a person, but she is so rattled that sudden sounds or movements send her into a panic.
A5170246.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She needs someone who understands fear-based reactivity, can give her the time and space to decompress without pressure, and will not startle her while she learns the world is not as dangerous as it feels right now. Ms Silly is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by close of business September 1st.

A5170428.name: Olive
bullets: Froze in the corner of her kennel the first day, eyes wide, body tight, not interested in food.
Flinched hard when the leash brushed her back, when anyone moved quickly, when handlers reached to remove equipment.
Paced and panted in the yard, drooling, wouldn't settle, sometimes followed handlers but backed away when they turned to face her.
Took treats gently through kennel bars on day two, allowed slow petting when handlers stayed still and kept their voices quiet.
Owner said high anxiety led to destructive behavior and house soiling at home despite knowing commands and being potty trained.
A5170428.story: Olive came in shut down and has stayed that way. She startles at touch, at movement, at the sound of other dogs, and spends her time either frozen or pacing. The previous owner had her four months, said she was diagnosed with high anxiety, and surrendered her when the stress showed up as destruction and accidents in the house. She knows there are people trying to help her but she cannot trust it yet.
A5170428.needs: Olive needs an experienced foster who understands fear this deep does not resolve in weeks, who will not push her, and who has a calm, quiet home with no children. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by close of business September 1st.

A5170402.name: Seven
bullets: Lived inside with three adults, one toddler, and two small female dogs since puppyhood—played and sniffed with the other dogs, no problems
Housetrained, alerts at the door, knows sit and kennel commands, crate trained with no issues
Owner surrendered for breed restrictions after five years—noted he doesn't like his ears touched and will air snap or growl, has an untreated ear infection in his right ear
In shelter has shown severe pain response and instability—trembling, falling repeatedly, leaning on handlers to stay upright, head tilt, delayed reactions
Growls and hard-stares when approached in kennel but has walked on leash to yard, did not seek interaction but used handler's leg for balance
A5170402.story: Seven spent five years in a home with small dogs and a young child before his family hit a breed restriction. He's now in a cement kennel with what appears to be a serious untreated medical condition—constant tremors, falling, leaning into people just to stand, a pronounced head tilt—and he is terrified. The fear and pain have made him defensive when cornered, but he has no bite history and walked on leash when given space to move.
A5170402.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Seven needs a New Hope partner rescue to pull him by close of business September 1st, and he needs someone who understands that pain makes dogs guard themselves. He needs veterinary assessment immediately and a foster who can give him quiet, time, and room to decompress while he heals.

A5169206.name: Julio
bullets: Found as a stray, walked nicely on leash in the shelter lobby
Saw a small dog at the vet when finder had him scanned for a chip—no reaction
In the yard finds a sunny spot, lies down, comes when called for treats and a little petting
Takes treats gently, walks on a loose leash, ignores dogs in nearby kennels
Wearing a cone after neuter made him hesitant and harder to read early on, but has been calm and solicited attention once settled
A5169206.story: Julio is a low-key two-year-old who would rather lounge in the sun than do much of anything else. Someone found him on a Phoenix street corner in late July, and nobody came looking. Now he has a respiratory infection that needs treatment outside the shelter, and he has seven days.
A5169206.needs: A quiet home with older kids at most, a slow introduction to the household, and a foster who can manage his medical care until he's well. He's listed as urgent medical with a September 3rd deadline.

A5164957.name: Cruisin
bullets: In the yard, walked soft on leash and checked in with handlers, accepted gentle petting on his head and leaned in when sitting at their feet
Shuts down hard when approached in the kennel—won't come forward, won't take treats from a hand, tucks and curls his lip when a leash appears
Flips his head back, pins his ears, and side-eyes when touched on his lower body or rear end
A5164957.story: Cruisin has two sides right now. In the yard with a patient handler, he's soft and sweet, leaning in for affection and taking treats gently. In the kennel, he's a different dog—frozen by fear, defensive, unable to let anyone close enough to leash him safely. Four months in this building and the pressure is breaking him down.
A5164957.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Cruisin needs an experienced handler who understands fear-based behavior and can give him the time and space to decompress outside of shelter conditions. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a partner rescue with the resources to support him. Deadline is September 2nd.

A5170107.name: Odyssey
bullets: Knew sit and shake, waited patiently for treats, solicited attention from handlers in the yard.
Walked on leash with mild pull, stopped to sniff, urinated and defecated normally.
Jumps up on people, bumps into handlers with force, struggles with body awareness.
Wary of leash initially, required adjustment to get comfortable with handling.
Bit someone who was trying to physically pull him through a barrier, puncture wounds.
A5170107.story: Odyssey is a three-year-old husky mix who knows basic commands and wants human attention, but his body is writing checks his impulse control can't cash. He jumps, he bumps, he moves through space like he doesn't know where he ends and you begin. When someone tried to physically move him past a barrier he didn't want to cross, he bit hard enough to break skin.
A5170107.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Odyssey needs an experienced handler who understands fearful, spatially unaware dogs and can teach him boundaries without force. Must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by close of business September 2.

A5170443.name: Sinclair
bullets: Found wandering at a gas station, rolled over for the finder and rode quietly in the car
In the shelter yard turned soft and wiggly, leaned into petting, flopped on her back for belly rubs, followed the handler around asking for attention
Terrified in the kennel—paces, hides, pancakes flat at the threshold—but once outside becomes submissive and affectionate
History of sudden, serious dog aggression in a previous environment: bit two dogs without warning, one requiring separation by blanket, the other by jumping a gate to reach
Lunged and pushed through barriers to get to cats
A5170443.story: Sinclair is a two-year-old cattle dog who shuts down hard in confinement but softens completely in open space, where she solicits touch and stays close. She has a documented history of severe attacks on other dogs and barrier-charging cats, both unpredictable and dangerous. Under that fear and those triggers is a dog who melts for human contact, but she needs someone who understands what they're looking at.
A5170443.needs: Only home with no other animals. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise—she requires an experienced handler who can manage serious dog aggression and predatory behavior toward cats. New Hope Only: Sinclair must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by close of business September 2nd.

A5167849.name: Sparrow
bullets: Wagged and pawed at the kennel door, leaned into handlers for petting, jumped onto laps asking for attention
Walked into the yard with a loose body, sniffed around independently, allowed petting and leash handling
Lunged and snapped at a handler through the kennel door when startled while resting in the back of the run
A5167849.story: Sparrow is a two-year-old dog who melts into affection once he trusts you—soft body, wagging tail, leaning in for touch. But when startled or approached before he's ready, he can escalate fast, teeth and all. He's been at West for two months and his window just closed to five days.
A5167849.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Sparrow needs an experienced handler who understands fear and can read what comes before the reaction. New Hope Only—he must be pulled by a partner rescue by September 2nd.

A5170216.name: Squirtle
bullets: Took treats through the kennel gate, then stepped back when the gate opened
Froze up when reached for, flinched hard when the leash came near
Once carried to the quiet room, paced some, then came forward for treats on his own terms
Became gentler taking treats as the session went on
Body goes stiff when a hand extends toward him—he needs space and predictability
A5170216.story: Squirtle is a 15-pound terrier mix carrying fear so heavy it makes him defensive when he feels cornered. He wants the treats, wants the connection, but his body locks up when people move too fast or reach without warning. In the shelter he has five days left and the clock is running.
A5170216.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Squirtle needs an experienced foster who understands fear-based reactivity, can move slowly, and won't push him past his threshold. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by close of business September 2nd.

A5170191.name: Snickers
bullets: Found with a friend, shares his kennel calmly, greets people with a quiet hello
Walks on a loose leash, takes treats gently, sat in a handler's lap for pets
Passed other dogs and shelter activity without pulling or reacting
A5170191.story: Snickers is a seven-year-old Chihuahua who ended up at East as a stray alongside another small dog. He's mellow for the breed—easy on leash, comfortable with handling, happy to lean into affection when it's offered. He has a heart murmur and an enlarged heart, which means he's on the medical priority list with six days left.
A5170191.needs: A foster who can manage a senior dog with a cardiac condition and get him to a vet soon after placement. Intake notes recommend going slow with new family introductions.

A5169032.name: Honey Bun
bullets: Approached a stranger in a neighborhood three weeks ago looking for attention, and has stayed soft and social with handlers ever since
After a week of fear shutdown—wouldn't eat, wouldn't move—she came back to herself: play bows, zoomies, then flops on your feet for belly rubs, then does it all over again
Takes treats gently, sits on cue, ignores other dogs when walking past kennels, pulls moderately on leash
A5169032.story: Honey Bun is a three-year-old pit mix who spent her first week at the shelter so shut down she wouldn't eat or walk, then woke up hilarious—bouncy and goofy and eager to be near people. She's been there six weeks now and has a respiratory infection that isn't clearing, which puts her at medical deadline in eleven days.
A5169032.needs: A foster home with no other pets for at least two weeks while she settles, then slow supervised introductions if there are resident dogs. She'll need leash work and a family introduction plan, and a foster who can give her the quiet she needs to finish healing. Medical priority—she leaves with treatment in progress.

A5170414.name: Becky
bullets: Came in with another dog on August 22, intake circumstances unknown
Showed tension in her kennel, but softened and sat quietly for petting once in a yard with a patient handler
Alarm-barked and air-snapped at a second person approaching, wary even after initial softening
Walked on leash with pulling and some environmental startle, tucked tail loosening up away from other dogs
A5170414.story: Becky is a seven-year-old shepherd mix carrying fear she can't quite set down. She warmed to one handler in the yard—sitting close, accepting touch all over, following with soft eyes—but a second person triggered alarm and a snap at the fence. She needs someone who understands that fear and reactivity are not the same as aggression, but they are still serious.
A5170414.needs: Experienced handler only, no other dogs, slow introductions to new people, and space to decompress without pressure. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. New Hope Only—Becky must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by September 2.

A5170154.name: Orson
bullets: Knows sit, takes treats gently, comes when called
Soft and happy approaching handlers in his kennel, accepts petting
Pulls hard on leash, fixates on other dogs—stiffens, stares, chuffs, low growls, won't disengage without handler intervention
Resisted returning to his kennel after seeing the dog next door, began pulling hard toward that kennel with stiff body
Paces and marks in play yard, tense body, takes time to settle before approaching handler
A5170154.story: Orson is a big, gentle-mouthed dog who knows basic commands and loves human attention. But he is also a dog whose reactivity to other dogs is escalating in the kennel, and the stress of confinement is showing in every movement—flagged tail, wide eyes, hard pulls, fixation he cannot break on his own. He needs out of this building.
A5170154.needs: Orson must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by close of business September 2nd. He needs an experienced handler and a home with no other dogs. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise.

A5169324.name: Mimosa
bullets: Found wandering with another dog, friendly and playful with her companion, allowed all handling from the stranger who picked her up
Timid in the shelter but softens when handlers give her time—eventually solicits attention, takes treats nicely, lets people pet her head and body
Lived briefly with young kids and was gentle and friendly with them, indifferent to cats, hasn't learned leash skills yet
Has had a persistent respiratory infection for weeks and is listed as urgent medical with ten days left
A5169324.story: Mimosa is a two-year-old pocket pit who came in scared and shut down after being found on the street, but she's showing more of herself as the days go on—wiggly when you talk soft, food motivated, sweet under the fear. She needs out now, both because she's running out of time and because she's been sick in there for a month.
A5169324.needs: A quiet home with someone who understands a shy dog needs space to decompress, plus commitment to follow-up vet care for her respiratory issue and patience with leash training from scratch. She'll need slow introductions to everything and everyone until she finds her footing.

A5170733.name: Dog A5170733
bullets: A senior tan Chihuahua who appeared at someone's door three days before intake and let himself be handled and carried
Approached shelter handlers with soft body and wagging tail, allowed petting and vaccines, trembled but tolerated all handling
Observed coughing at intake, flagged for multiple medical concerns and on medical priority with two days left
A5170733.story: This 12-year-old showed up alone at a stranger's house and stayed, which tells you something about how tired he was. He's gentle with people and scared, and the shelter has serious concerns about his health.
A5170733.needs: Must be pulled by a registered New Hope Partner rescue no later than September 3rd. Needs a foster prepared for senior medical care and the costs that come with it, and a quiet place while he's evaluated and treated.

A4670415.name: Jack
bullets: Fourteen-year-old cattle dog who knows sit, walks on leash, and is housetrained
Lived with another dog for the last four months and got along well, relaxed and friendly with handlers at intake
Came in because his person went into permanent care and the temporary caretaker could not keep him long-term
Greets people calmly, takes treats gently, described as medium to low energy
Startles at fireworks but otherwise steady
A4670415.story: Jack spent most of his life with someone who is now in a facility and cannot come home. The friend who tried to bridge the gap could only manage four months. Now Jack is fourteen, medically fragile, and running out of road at a shelter with a medical deadline.
A4670415.needs: Jack must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than end of business September 8th. He needs a quiet foster home that understands senior dogs with medical needs and will not ask him to be anything other than what he is at the end of a long life.

A5170726.name: Dog A5170726
bullets: Took treats gently at first, then mouthier as he relaxed; knows 'sit' for treats
Came when called in the yard, leaned against handler's lap for petting, explored with soft tail wag
Walked slowly on leash with verbal coaxing, lowered his head when handler reached to remove it
A5170726.story: This five-year-old brown and white staffy mix is moving carefully through the shelter, watching people closely before he decides they're safe. Once he knows you, he softens—comes over, leans in, takes the comfort he can get. He's on the medical priority list and has seven days.
A5170726.needs: Must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than September 8th. Needs a calm, patient home that will give him time to settle and access to whatever medical support he requires. Intake notes say go slow.

A5170784.name: Dog A5170784
bullets: Seven-year-old, 18-pound terrier mix who spent three days in a finder's home staying calm in a crate, relaxed most of the time, low energy.
Dismissed both the children and the other dogs in that home—didn't engage, didn't react, just kept to herself.
Came to the front of her kennel when called at the shelter, allowed petting and handling without trouble.
A5170784.story: She was found wandering near a park with another dog, and the picture that emerges is of a senior who has turned inward. She accepted what happened around her but didn't ask for much. The shelter has flagged multiple medical issues and placed her on medical priority.
A5170784.needs: Must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than end of business September 8. She needs a quiet foster home with someone who understands older dogs carrying things the intake paperwork can't name, and the patience to let her surface at her own pace.

A4670414.name: Shadow
bullets: At 14, Shadow walks on leash, knows sit, takes treats gently, and has lived peacefully with another dog.
Staff note a loose wiggly body, tail wagging, attention whines at kennel front, and that she accepts petting and handling.
She came to the shelter after four months with someone caring for a friend's dogs—the friend entered permanent care and could not take the dogs back.
Housebroken, lived both indoors and out, limited to the kitchen when left alone.
Medical priority flag, geriatric with multiple medical issues on record.
A4670414.story: Shadow is 14 and a half and still greets handlers with a wagging tail and a soft ask for attention. She ended up here through no fault of her own—passed from one temporary situation to the next when her original owner could no longer care for her. She deserves a soft place to land for whatever time she has left.
A4670414.needs: A quiet home prepared for senior medical needs and end-of-life care, with someone who understands this is a hospice commitment, not a long-term fostering situation. Shadow is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business September 8.

A5170754.name: Frank
bullets: Six-month-old pup found wandering a parking lot, jumped right into a stranger's car
Soft and wiggly with staff, allows all handling and petting, knows sit
Mouthy and jumpy in the normal puppy way, high energy, walked on leash without trouble
Rode in a car with a four-month-old baby without reacting or paying the child attention
Has a fractured left hind leg that will require surgery or amputation
A5170754.story: Frank is a young pit bull mix who trusted the wrong situation and ended up lost. He has the typical puppy menu—mouthy, bouncy, eager—and the easy social confidence of a dog who has been handled. The leg fracture happened before intake and the clock is running.
A5170754.needs: Frank needs a partner rescue to pull him by end of business September 9th. He will need surgical repair or amputation and the months of recovery and foster care that follow. This is a medical case with a hard deadline.

A5170480.name: Castor
bullets: Found as a stray, approached a family on his own, let them handle him and bring him inside for the night
Knows sit, walks well on leash, comfortable with a harness, used to living indoors with freedom to roam
Freezes and stiffens when walking past kennels, reacts to nearby dogs with barking and pulling toward fences
Showed teeth and growled when handler tried to scan for a microchip, and when touched while eating
Will approach for attention in the yard, follows handlers around, takes treats but can be grabby
A5170480.story: Castor walked up to a stranger's house looking for help, friendly enough to get himself taken in for the night. But the shelter has rattled him. He freezes near barking dogs, escalates when startled or crowded, and has made it clear he does not want to be touched during certain moments. Underneath the tension is a dog who knows how to live in a home and will follow you around a quiet yard.
A5170480.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Castor needs an experienced handler who understands pressure and thresholds, a home without other animals, and space to decompress without being pushed. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue no later than September 8th.

A5169764.name: Durian
bullets: Approached a stranger and his dog wanting to play, allowed petting and handling
Knows sit, down, and shake; stays close in the yard and leans in for affection
Food motivated, takes treats nicely, ignores barking dogs when walking past kennels
Pulls hard on leash but settles when redirected; seems housetrained
Kennel stress is high—whines, demand barks, paws at the leash—but outside the kennel he's soft-bodied, affectionate, and calm
A5169764.story: Durian was found as a stray at 55th and Indian School, friendly and playful with the finder's dog. He's a young Lab mix who knows basic commands and craves human contact, but a month in a kennel is grinding him down. Outside his run, handlers see a different dog: sweet, gentle, eager to be near people.
A5169764.needs: Experienced home that understands decompression and can give him time and space to recover from shelter stress. He's behaviorally sound but not a beginner's dog. Deadline is September 8.

A5170544.name: Duse
bullets: Crate trained, house trained, alerts at the door when he needs out
Walks on leash with strong pull; at the shelter he is tense and shut down, paces, flinches at touch, will not settle or take treats
In his previous home, lunged at a running toddler and knocked him over; owner reports low patience around young children
Reactive to male dogs, began escalating with the male dog in his home; fine with the female dog he lived with
Guards his food bowl with low growls and loud barking if disturbed while eating
A5170544.story: Duse is a two-year-old intact male who lived in a crowded household with six adults, two young children, and two smaller dogs. His tolerance wore thin: he knocked over a running two-year-old when the child charged at him, escalated with the male dog in the home, and guarded his food. At the shelter he is terrified, cowering, trembling, flinching at noise and touch, pulling erratically to avoid going back in his kennel.
A5170544.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Duse needs an adult-only home with no other dogs, someone who understands resource guarding and fear, and who will not rush him. He is New Hope Only, meaning he must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue with the experience to evaluate him safely outside the shelter and provide the long-term foster placement he needs.

A5169130.name: Einstein
bullets: Walks on a loose leash, takes treats gently, and puts his front paws on your knees when he wants attention.
Curious about other dogs when walking past kennels, though he doesn't care for barking.
Shuts down when nervous but softens when someone speaks quietly and gives him time.
Has been at the shelter since late July and is currently battling kennel cough.
Needs a home with no children.
A5169130.story: Einstein is a twenty-pound poodle mix who knows how to ask for what he needs—he'll put his paws on your knees and wait. He's been in the shelter for over a month now, fighting off kennel cough, and he has six days left to find a way out. When he's scared, he freezes and watches, but when you give him space and speak softly, he comes back to himself.
A5169130.needs: A quiet adult-only home where he can decompress without pressure, with someone who understands that a dog who goes still needs patience, not pushing. He's on a medical deadline because of unresolved kennel cough, so he needs a foster who can get him out by September 8th and give him time to heal somewhere calmer than this.

A5170403.name: Kiwi
bullets: Found wandering, stayed three days with a finder who reported she hunched low and whimpered around their large dog but eventually relaxed enough to sniff and play with kids.
In the shelter she sits in the back corner trembling, won't approach, and shuts down hard when handlers reach for her.
Handlers report she growls, bares teeth, thrashes, and vocalizes when they try to leash or move her—classic terror response from a ten-pound dog with nowhere to go.
A5170403.story: Kiwi is a two-year-old Chihuahua who was skittish but warming up in a home, then landed in a concrete kennel and broke. She's not aggressive—she's flooded with fear. She needs someone who understands that small scared dogs bite when cornered, and who won't corner her.
A5170403.needs: Experienced small-dog foster who knows how to give a shutdown dog space and time, no young kids, quiet home. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. New Hope Only: Kiwi must be pulled by a registered partner rescue no later than September 8th.

A5170890.name: Dog A5170890
bullets: Lifted his head slowly when his handler approached, made eye contact with soft eyes, accepted petting
Walks on leash, takes treats gently, allowed full handling and vaccines with light restraint
81 pounds, eight years old, currently in the West shelter medical wing
A5170890.story: This senior German Shepherd is quiet and gentle with people who give him time. He's in the shelter's medical wing with multiple age-related conditions, and the clock is running.
A5170890.needs: Must be pulled by a registered New Hope Partner rescue no later than September 8th. Needs a foster home prepared for senior dog care and whatever medical support comes with eight years of wear. This is not a beginner's dog.

A5169494.name: Rex
bullets: Walks on a loose leash and stays calm around other dogs in kennels, curious but not reactive
Settles into handling after a shy start, then relaxes and engages with people
Takes treats gently, greets handlers with soft body language and tail wags
A5169494.story: Rex has been at East Shelter for a month with a respiratory infection that hasn't resolved. Handlers describe him as calm and gentle once he warms up—a dog who follows you around the yard and leans in for affection once he knows you're safe.
A5169494.needs: A foster who can give him time to settle in and continue the medical care he needs for his respiratory illness. He has six days to find that placement.

A5170383.name: Tolliver
bullets: Solicited attention from both handlers in the yard, sat when asked, took treats gently, leaned against them for petting while carrying a toy
Chased after toys and walked on leash with a strong pull, marked frequently, wandered the space and checked in with people
Became very distressed when it was time to return to the kennel, pulled away from the door, thrashed on leash, would not go back in willingly
A5170383.story: Tolliver is a three-year-old cattle dog mix who likes people and will play and take direction when he's out of his kennel. But something about going back into that space has become unbearable for him, and the resistance is escalating. He needs out now, before the walls close in any tighter.
A5170383.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Tolliver needs an experienced foster through a New Hope partner rescue who can pull him by September 8th and work with him in a home environment where the pressure comes off and someone can see who he actually is. He showed reactivity to another dog passing the yard, so a dog-savvy home is essential.

A5169725.name: Amethyst
bullets: Loves being with people—wiggly, affectionate, jumps in laps, asks for petting and closes her eyes when she gets it
Plays fetch enthusiastically, runs back with the toy, knows sit and drop it
Resource guards toys when handlers reach toward them—low growled once, air snapped when a handler tried to pick up a toy she had
A5169725.story: Amethyst is a velcro dog who wants nothing more than to be close to her person. She's playful and responsive, but she struggles with impulse control and has begun to guard objects in the stressful shelter environment. The staff has seen enough to know she needs space and skilled handling to show what she's capable of.
A5169725.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. She needs an experienced handler who understands resource guarding and can give her structure, consistency, and time to decompress. She must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than close of business September 8.

A5170304.name: Bandit
bullets: Bandit is a year-old Lab mix who pulls hard on leash and has high energy that quickly tips into over-arousal—handlers saw him escalate from playing with toys to panting heavily with a glassy look, needing constant redirection to stay engaged.
He's mouthy with leashes and hands when excited, snapping at the leash during handling and mouthing toward handlers' hands, though he redirects to toys and accepts petting when calm.

Came in as a stray the previous owners couldn't locate, then lived outside for three months with minimal training—he's crate trained but not housebroken, dismissive of the toddler in that home, and had no contact with other animals there.
Shelter handlers use a two-person rotation with toys to manage his jumping and leash-biting; he plays in the yard, jumps in the water pool, but doesn't play fetch or take treats when amped up.
Barks and jumps at his kennel gate, tried to fence-fight a neighboring dog, and stress-urinated during a meet-and-greet when getting pets.
A5170304.story: Bandit is a young dog with a motor that runs too hot and no off switch yet. He's not mean—he settles for petting, he plays, he redirects—but he doesn't know how to manage his own intensity, and the shelter can't teach him that in a concrete run.
A5170304.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Bandit needs an experienced handler who understands arousal and can build structure without confrontation, a home with no young children, and space to burn energy in ways that don't wind him tighter. He is New Hope Only, so only a qualified partner rescue can pull him by close of business September 8th.

A5170609.name: Billie
bullets: Found wandering with another dog in late August; the finder said both dogs allowed petting and handling from adults and children
When evaluated in the shelter, stood tense and watchful, startled easily, but learned to take treats from hand and demonstrated 'sit' command
Walked on leash with awareness and caution, showed interest in calm dogs she passed, relieved herself outside
In the yard with a patient handler, eventually lay down nearby and leaned in briefly when petted slowly on the head
Demonstrates low tolerance for handling in the kennel environment and needs space to decompress
A5170609.story: Billie is a two-year-old brown and white dog who came in scared and has stayed that way. She knows some things—sit, leash, how to be near a person who moves slowly—but the shelter has her wound tight. In a quieter place, with time, she might show you who she was before this.
A5170609.needs: Billie needs an experienced handler who understands fear and will not rush her, in a calm home without young children. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with the capacity to support her through decompression and further evaluation.

A4874882.name: Griso
bullets: Resource guards his food from other dogs—growls, snarls, shows teeth if they come too close while he's eating
Growls at children if they approach too quickly, and his family says don't let kids pick him up
Cuddly and friendly with the people he knows and trusts, but deeply fearful of strangers and new situations

A4874882.story: Griso spent seven years with his family before a neighbor's dog kept breaking into their yard and attacking their dogs, and they couldn't keep him safe anymore. In the shelter he is terrified—barking at handlers from the corner, trembling when touched, shutting down completely—but his family says at home he was affectionate and cuddly with the people he trusted.
A4874882.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Griso needs an experienced, patient adult home with no children, no other dogs, and someone who understands fear-based behavior and resource guarding. He is New Hope Only, which means he must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue.

A5170555.story: Peanut is a young dog carrying fear so heavy it looks like aggression until you wait long enough to see what's underneath. He doesn't know yet that a leash means a walk, that a hand means kindness, but in a yard with a calm handler he remembered how to be a puppy—wiggly, leaning in, asking for more. He's 11 months old and out of time in a place that terrifies him.
A5170555.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Peanut needs an experienced foster with a rescue partner who understands fear-based behavior, can move slowly, won't take the growling personally, and has the time to let him learn the world isn't dangerous. New Hope Only—he must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by end of day September 8.

Gets very excited at the kennel gate after being inside all day—jumps, paws, pushes—then settles once the leash is on and he can move.
A5166643.story: Rocko is a young dog who had almost no life before this. Two weeks in a crate outside, then impounded when he tried to jump the fence and snapped when someone grabbed his harness. In the shelter yard with space to move, he shows what he actually is: energetic, affectionate, toy-motivated, responsive to calm direction.
A5166643.needs: Needs an experienced, active home that understands a dog with this start will take time, structure, and daily exercise to decompress and learn how to live inside. This is not a beginner's dog. New Hope Only—must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of business September 8th.
